promptText: Given an array of integers, find two numbers that add up to a given target. Explain your approach and its time complexity.
ioFormat: Line 1: space-separated integers (the array). Line 2: the target integer. Print the two 0-indexed positions whose values sum to the target, space-separated, in ascending order of index.

promptText: Reverse a singly linked list. Walk through your approach.
ioFormat: Line 1: space-separated integers representing the linked list values in order. Print the reversed list as space-separated integers on one line.

promptText: What is the difference between a stack and a queue, and give a real use case for each.
What is the average-case time complexity of searching for an element in a hash map?
explanation: A well-distributed hash map gives O(1) average-case lookup; worst case can degrade to O(n) with heavy collisions.

promptText: Given a string, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Explain your approach.
ioFormat: Line 1: a string. Print a single integer: the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

promptText: Given a binary tree, determine if it is height-balanced. Explain your approach and complexity.
ioFormat: Line 1: level-order traversal of the binary tree, space-separated integers, using 'N' for a null child. Print 'true' if the tree is height-balanced, else 'false'.

promptText: Explain the difference between BFS and DFS, and describe a scenario where you'd prefer one over the other.
Which sorting algorithm has the best worst-case time complexity?
explanation: Merge sort guarantees O(n log n) in the worst case; quicksort can degrade to O(n^2), and bubble/insertion sort are O(n^2) in the worst case.

promptText: Given a list of intervals, merge all overlapping intervals. Explain your approach and its time complexity.
ioFormat: Line 1: number of intervals n. Next n lines: two space-separated integers 'start end' per interval. Print the merged intervals, one per line, as 'start end', sorted by start.

promptText: Design an algorithm to find the median of two sorted arrays in O(log(min(m,n))) time.
ioFormat: Line 1: space-separated integers for the first sorted array (blank line if empty). Line 2: space-separated integers for the second sorted array. Print the median as a floating point number (e.g. 2.0 or 2.5).

promptText: Explain how a trie works and describe a real-world system where it would outperform a hash map.
